freshness_caveat: Coal data (96 USD/t) is 220 days stale (as of 2025-12-26); Clean Dark (27.95 EUR/MWh) is 215 days stale (as of 2025-12-31). Current analysis uses fresh power, gas, storage, and renewable data (as of 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-03) but coal-based merit order shifts should be treated with caution.
risk_flags: Paks 1.9 GW baseload loss forces Hungarian imports; HUPX/PXE spreads at risk of sharp widening.
EU storage at 57.1% (32nd pctile, 16.3 pp below seasonal) limits flexibility for summer heat or supply shocks.
Spain/France wildfire threat to Iberian thermal and hydro generation; transmission corridor risk high.
DE Power at 78th pctile (146.32 EUR/MWh) and GB Power at 90th pctile (134.06 EUR/MWh) indicate tightness; coal at 7th pctile (96 USD/t) may not support further thermal dispatch.

base.summary: Paks offline, storage deficit managed; power remains elevated (DE 140–150, GB 130–140); TTF steady 58–61 EUR/MWh on seasonal gas draw.

downside.summary: Paks returns within days; cooler weather reduces AC demand; Mexico LNG ramp accelerates, softening US arb; Hormuz de-escalates.

upside.summary: Danube drought spreads to Kozloduy (Bulgaria) or further east EU nuclear; wildfire expansion into French hydro; Hormuz escalation spike crude premium.

themes: Central EU nuclear outage and drought cascades
Iberian wildfire risk to thermal and hydro
Hormuz premium persists, LNG arb softens
top_drivers: Paks nuclear offline (~1.9 GW) forces Central EU thermal dispatch and import competition, tightening regional and German power spreads.
EU storage 16.3 pp below seasonal (57.1% full) constrains summer flexibility; any demand or supply shock will test gas balancing and TTF forward curve.
Spain/France wildfire threat erodes Iberian thermal and hydro; drought-driven cascade across Danube basin pressures multi-hub generation margins.
Mexico LNG ramp-up (0.4 Bcf/d) reduces US-EU arbitrage incentive; Hormuz tension sustains crude premium but lacks coalition support for escalation.
top_takeaway: Hungary's Paks nuclear plant offline amid Danube drought; EU storage 16.3 pp below seasonal drives gas and power upside in Central/SW Europe.

watchlist.metric: Paks outage duration and Hungarian demand response
watchlist.why: 1.9 GW baseload loss drives Central EU hub premiums and may spillover to Germany via corridor flows.

watchlist.metric: Danube water levels and nuclear cooling thresholds
watchlist.why: Further drought risk widens outage cascade across central/eastern EU; pressures gas balancing.

watchlist.metric: Spain/France wildfire perimeter and thermal outages
watchlist.why: Each MW of Iberian generation loss tightens SW EU power and lifts TTF spreads; hydro margin erosion bullish for gas.
At 57.1%, seasonal deficit limits headroom; any demand spike or supply loss (Hormuz, LNG diversion) will test storage draw risk.

watchlist.metric: Mexico LNG (Energia Costa Azul) export ramp-up
watchlist.why: 0.4 Bcf/d new capacity softens US Henry Hub arb, reduces EU LNG imports, marginal bearish for TTF Q3–Q4.

watchlist.metric: Strait of Hormuz escalation and allied coalition
watchlist.why: Weak coalition backing elevates duration of Strait premium; impacts crude-to-LNG arb and Med/NW diversion flows.
